exposure: Confirmed diagnosis of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM)
Mode of birth (cesarean section vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery)
outcome: Postpartum type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) screening uptake
cohort: The study included 642 nondiabetic women with a confirmed diagnosis of GDM, who were followed until delivery at a tertiary care center.
finding: The study identified a substantial gap in postpartum T2DM screening among women with GDM, with only 20.2% effectively screened, despite a high incidence (13.9%) of post-GDM T2DM among those screened.
mod_finding: Women who had cesarean sections were more likely to take postpartum T2DM screening (25.0%) compared to those with spontaneous vaginal delivery (16.5%), and post-GDM T2DM was associated with spontaneous vaginal delivery (20.6% vs. 7.6% for cesarean section).
followup_time: N/A (followed until delivery, and postpartum screening/diagnosis)
